clue.text: Remove wet medic with prickly exterior

indicators.note: with a prickly exterior says the spiny word forms the outside, wrapping round the medic
with a prickly exterior says the spiny word forms the outside, wrapping round the medic

parts.note: prickly means spiny, covered in spines
DR is the abbreviation for doctor, a medic

explanation.surface: A doctor with a bristly manner is told to sort out something damp.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinning laundry fast in a machine flings water out, so it is a way to take away wetness.

clue.text: Adapted transport framework, Caledonian, headed northwards

indicators.note: headed means a letter is sent to the head of the word, here the S from the Scot
in a down clue, going northwards means reading the pieces from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: a rack is a framework for holding things
Caledonia is the old Latin name for Scotland, so a Caledonian is a Scot

explanation.surface: A modified vehicle's frame is made by a Scot who has driven north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'northwards' reverses RACK and SCOT to give TOCSKCAR; 'headed' then moves the S to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A stock car is an ordinary saloon modified for rough-and-tumble track racing, so it is transport that has been altered.

clue.text: Solvent abuse finally suppressed by cross unknown man

indicators.note: in a down clue, being suppressed by something means sitting underneath it, so this letter comes after the others

parts.note: a cross is the letter X
Y is one of the algebraic unknowns
Len is a man's name

indicators.note: finally picks out the last letter of the word abuse

explanation.surface: A cross man puts a stop to solvent abuse.
explanation.definitionFit: Xylene is an aromatic hydrocarbon widely used as an industrial solvent and paint thinner.

clue.text: British ultimately ruin safari, upsetting Africans

indicators.note: upsetting means knocking the letters over into a new order
ultimately picks out the final letter of the word ruin

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: British tourists spoil a safari, offending the local Africans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' rearranges N (the end of 'ruin') with SAFARI to make IAFRANS.
explanation.definitionFit: Biafrans were people of the Nigerian region that broke away as Biafra in 1967, so they are an example of Africans.

clue.text: Old soldier, a camp commander?

definitions.meaning: British infantrymen once wore scarlet tunics and were nicknamed for them
at Butlin's holiday camps in Britain the staff who organise the guests' fun wear red jackets

explanation.surface: A veteran is asked whether he once ran a military camp.
explanation.walkthrough: Butlin's is a chain of British holiday camps whose entertainment staff are famous for their red jackets; the question mark flags the playful 'commander'.
explanation.definitionFit: The name was used for British soldiers in scarlet uniform and is still used for Butlin's holiday-camp hosts.

clue.text: Way to stop another week disappearing — can't be bothered with this

indicators.note: to stop means to plug a gap, so the path sits inside the other letters
disappearing says the week's letter vanishes from the word

parts.note: another refers back to the clue's first word, so another way
a path is a way

explanation.surface: Someone too listless to keep the weeks from slipping away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' is a second WAY; with W gone ('disappearing') it is AY, which PATH plugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Apathy is the state of indifference in which nothing seems worth the effort.

clue.text: Stems from him getting zero when playing spades

indicators.note: playing means the letters are toyed with and put in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: 'when playing' rearranges HIM and ZERO to make RHIZOME.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhizome is a creeping underground stem, as in ginger or iris.

clue.text: Revival of second addict on return call

indicators.note: on return means the pieces come back the other way, read from the end

explanation.walkthrough: 'on return' reverses S and USER to give RESUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Resuscitation is bringing someone back to life or consciousness, the same idea as revival.

clue.text: Sumo wrestler thrown over in strike zone

indicators.note: thrown over says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

explanation.walkthrough: The letters IKEZO sit inside 'strike zone'; 'thrown over' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: Ozeki is the second-highest rank in sumo, just below yokozuna, so it names a wrestler of that grade.

clue.text: One hiding in rocks removing a pair of pants

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'pants' means underpants, and 'knackers' is vulgar slang for testicles.
explanation.definitionFit: Knickers are women's underpants, a plural garment like trousers, so a pair of pants in British usage.

clue.text: Fine to soak topless people

explanation.surface: Topless bathers get a fine soaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' drops the D from DRENCH; the surface hints at nude sunbathing.

clue.text: Nutty, fruity biscuits not all there

definitions.meaning: fruity can mean eccentric or mad, as in a fruitcake
crispbreads and savoury biscuits eaten with cheese

explanation.surface: Some fruit-and-nut biscuits are missing from the tin.
explanation.walkthrough: Four definitions of one word; the surface pretends 'Nutty, fruity' describe the biscuits.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang the word means mad, matching nutty, fruity and not all there, and it is also the name for thin crisp savoury biscuits.

clue.text: Brute, obsessive and obstinate about vacuous idealism

explanation.walkthrough: 'obsessive and obstinate' together describe one word, the slang short form of anal-retentive; 'vacuous' means emptied of its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A brute is a beast, any non-human creature, and also a coarse person called a beast.

clue.text: Extremely fast leak spanning break, I think

explanation.walkthrough: 'take a leak' is slang for urinating; IMO = in my opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: Prestissimo is the musical direction for the very fastest tempo.

clue.text: Literally strap a problem for links

explanation.surface: Literally, a strap is a problem on the golf course.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: an S together with TRAP makes the word 'strap'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bunker of sand on a golf course is a hazard golfers dread, and links are seaside golf courses.
